title: Scoped tenant configuration recovery after a simulated malicious change
purpose: Recover only explicitly named disposable configuration objects and their relationships from a trusted external baseline, without treating native object recovery as full tenant, credential, application-data or relationship recovery.

scope.permittedTarget: An approved isolated tenant with disposable policies, groups, application/service-principal relationships and synthetic users named in a written change plan.
scope.notAClaim: This is a scoped recovery design. Native coverage, retention, object lifecycle, licensing and source-of-authority limits must be checked for the exact tenant/product version. A recovered object is not proof its relationships or security state were restored.
excluded: Restoring untrusted credentials, malicious consent or compromised policy
Assuming baseline exports contain secrets or application data

sourceReferences.qualification: The source authority's 2026-11-18 check reports Standard P1/P2 retention up to 7 days and Premium preview pay-as-you-go up to 30 days, with no native recreation of hard-deleted objects and hybrid-source limitations. Recheck exact current coverage, eligibility and retention before any approved reliance.
Independent recovery administration and baseline custody cannot require the suspected compromised identity chain or an available ITSM service.

prerequisites.requirement: Approval identifies the isolated tenant, disposable object IDs/types, allowable mutations, relationship grants, restore mechanism, time window and rollback owner.
prerequisites.evidence: Approved object/relationship allow-list and change plan.

prerequisites.requirement: Independent clean recovery administration is available and the suspected compromised path is excluded from baseline custody and approval.
prerequisites.evidence: Authorized R1 evidence, clean workstation attestation, custodian access test.

prerequisites.requirement: Known-good baseline predates the simulated change and includes provenance, immutable/versioned history, signed approval or independently held hash and access records.
prerequisites.evidence: Baseline manifest, version/date/hash, independent approval and custody record.

prerequisites.requirement: Per-object coverage and retention matrix records soft/hard deletion, hybrid authority, writable attributes, license/preview constraints and unsupported relationship/credential gaps.
prerequisites.evidence: Current source sections plus actual lab product/version/retention observations.

prerequisites.requirement: Relationship graph includes app↔service principal, group membership, owners, role assignments, API grants/consent, Conditional Access targets/exclusions and application-specific authorization references.
prerequisites.evidence: Baseline directed graph and a reviewed recreation order/ID-mapping template.

prerequisites.requirement: Approval defines semantic acceptance, negative tests, RTO/RPO and how unrelated legitimate changes will be preserved.
prerequisites.evidence: Per-object expected diff, tests, rollback snapshots and independent witness plan.

coverageMatrix.plannedMethod: Use native recovery only where the current product coverage and deletion window explicitly permit it.
coverageMatrix.gap: Object types, attributes, retention and eligibility differ; native retention is not long-term baseline custody.

coverageMatrix.objectOrRelation: Hard-deleted objects or unsupported object types
coverageMatrix.plannedMethod: If approved and technically supported, recreate from external desired state with new IDs; otherwise declare unrecoverable and use application-specific recovery.
coverageMatrix.gap: No promise of native hard-deleted-object recreation; immutable IDs may change and dependent references must be remapped.

coverageMatrix.plannedMethod: Restore through the authoritative source using its separately approved procedure, then verify synchronization.
coverageMatrix.gap: Cloud overwrite is not a substitute for source-of-authority recovery.

coverageMatrix.objectOrRelation: Groups, owners, role assignments, CA target/exclusion references
coverageMatrix.plannedMethod: Reconcile every allow-listed edge against the trusted graph after object recovery; manually reconstruct unsupported approved relationships through their supported administration path.
coverageMatrix.gap: Object existence does not prove memberships, ownership, permissions or policy references are restored. The checked native property scope excludes user manager/sponsor changes, group-owner changes and dynamic membership rule changes; recheck current coverage rather than assuming these return with an object.

coverageMatrix.objectOrRelation: Application registration, service principal, consent and external app authorization
coverageMatrix.plannedMethod: Recreate approved components in dependency order and obtain fresh explicit consent/authorization only for baseline privileges.
coverageMatrix.gap: Cross-object IDs, tenant-local service principals and application data/roles require independent checks; never restore attacker grants.

coverageMatrix.objectOrRelation: Secrets, keys, authentication methods and sessions
coverageMatrix.plannedMethod: Rotate/re-enroll with approved custodians and revoke applicable sessions rather than export or restore secret values from JSON.
coverageMatrix.gap: Baseline configuration is not credential recovery; rotation and revocation effects are service-specific.

coverageMatrix.plannedMethod: Use separately retained logs and workload-specific backup/restore procedures.
coverageMatrix.gap: Tenant configuration recovery does not recreate lost logs, mailboxes, documents, databases or an entire tenant.

dependencyLimits.dependency: Independent administration, Entra service and target APIs
dependencyLimits.failureBehavior: If unavailable, preserve evidence and escalate; the baseline alone cannot restore access.

dependencyLimits.dependency: Trusted pre-compromise baseline and external integrity/custody anchor
dependencyLimits.failureBehavior: Do not restore an untrusted export or use a hash stored only beside an attacker-writable baseline as authenticity proof.
Pause dependent application access until all required edges are remapped and unauthorized edges denied.

dependencyLimits.dependency: Source authority, native coverage and retention
dependencyLimits.failureBehavior: Use the correct source or approved recreation path; unsupported recovery remains an explicit gap.

steps.action: Check isolated scope, rollback owner and approval; record incident/exercise time, freeze only approved synthetic changes, and preserve pre-exercise state and logs.
steps.expected: No real tenant incident or broader freeze is induced; trustworthy before-state exists.

steps.action: Retrieve the baseline through independent custody, verify its approved provenance and immutable version, and compare its date to the simulated compromise point.
steps.expected: Baseline is known-good independently of the exercised tenant; it contains no secret material.
steps.onFailure: Do not restore; classify baseline trust as failed/unknown.

steps.action: Verify independent administration and read current object/relationship state using only approved privileges.
steps.expected: Clean recovery path and explicit actual-versus-baseline semantic diff are available.
steps.onFailure: Stop; do not broaden privilege or use suspected compromised credentials.

steps.action: Recheck the coverage matrix, actual object deletion state, applicable retention, source authority and product eligibility. Select native recovery, supported recreation or declared unsupported for each object.
steps.expected: No object is restored on an assumed coverage/retention claim.
steps.onFailure: Mark unsupported/unrecoverable items and stop changes that need them.

steps.action: Apply the separately approved benign synthetic mutation to the disposable targets only, or observe the prearranged fixture state. Preserve resulting IDs/audit events; do not simulate actual malicious credentials or persistence.
steps.expected: Only expected scoped drift exists and it is observable.
steps.onFailure: Stop and restore pre-exercise baseline using approved rollback.

steps.action: Recover/recreate parent objects using the selected supported methods; keep applications quarantined from unintended grants. Record old→new IDs without secret values.
steps.expected: Required allow-listed objects and intended writable attributes match desired state.
steps.onFailure: Pause dependent actions; retain partial recovery and errors.

steps.action: Recreate only independently approved baseline relationships in order: owners, group members, app↔service-principal links, necessary role/API assignments, explicit consent and CA targets/exclusions. Remap every changed ID.
steps.expected: All intended edges exist, unintended privilege edges are absent, and no attacker or stale grant is restored.
steps.onFailure: Leave affected app access contained and remove only the approved erroneous synthetic edge.

steps.action: If credentials/methods are within approved scope, rotate/re-enroll them and reconcile revocation; otherwise mark this component not exercised and do not claim credential recovery.
steps.expected: No compromised secret is restored; acceptance clearly identifies remaining session/credential exposure.
steps.onFailure: Do not release the dependent application to use.

steps.action: Run fresh positive and negative access tests for every required relationship and policy target, including an unauthorized synthetic principal and removed old-ID references.
steps.expected: Intended access works and unintended/stale access is denied; object existence alone is insufficient.
steps.onFailure: Keep recovery failed/partial and contain the scoped app.

steps.action: Compare the final semantic object+edge diff, logs and elapsed recovery/baseline age to approved acceptance. Check unrelated legitimate settings remained unchanged.
steps.expected: RTO/RPO are measured; every gap, failed edge and untested object is visible.
steps.onFailure: Reject release/claim of completion and choose approved rollback or further remediation.

steps.action: Restore the approved pre-exercise synthetic state as required by the plan, verify it again, and retain all evidence in independent versioned storage.
steps.expected: Exercise end state is explicitly approved, reversible and auditable.
steps.onFailure: Escalate scoped cleanup and preserve the failed result.

trigger: Unsupported restore or unexplained object/edge diff
steps: Freeze approved exercise actions and preserve partial state, event IDs and ID mappings.
Choose the separately trusted pre-exercise snapshot, not an attacker-modified current export.
Revert only allow-listed synthetic objects/edges in dependency order; never blindly overwrite unrelated legitimate changes.
Verify positive/negative access and final graph; leave unsupported components contained and escalate.
acceptance: No unintended grants or stale references
Independent admin and evidence access retained
Unrecoverable and untested components explicitly accepted or left blocked

passCriteria: Per-object supported method and retention established
Intended object attributes and all required directed relationships restored
Fresh positive/negative access tests pass, including old-ID/removed-grant denial
No unapproved privilege or unrelated change
RTO/RPO and rollback measured within approved bounds
failCriteria: Native restore coverage or retention assumed
Hard-deleted recovery claimed without supported recreation evidence
Untrusted credentials or malicious grants restored
Unproven rollback or unknown unrelated impact
evidenceRequirements: RTO/RPO, rollback, gap register and independent acceptance

expected: Actual scoped restoration and relationship recreation tested in a separately authorized isolated tenant, with fresh positive/negative acceptance and rollback.
validation.blocker: Only local fixtures/browser tests are authorized. No tenant object mutation, recovery or relationship grant is authorized.
